Running work no longer blocks a switch that doesn't need to wait. Installed on the owner's PC and both paths used live before release.

**What changed**

- **Claude switches go through at once.** With the Claude provider 0.3.1 or later, a Claude-only switch no longer waits for Hermes to be idle and no longer turns messages away, even while a session is working. Every chat uses the new Claude account from its next message.
- **Codex switches wait instead of refusing.** If Hermes is working, a Codex switch now waits for the running work to finish, checking twice a second, so it goes ahead the moment Hermes is free. The window shows "Waiting for the current reply to finish" meanwhile. New messages sent during that wait are turned away; send them again.
- **Known limit:** the Codex wait gives up after one minute. A long agent session, one that keeps running commands, can outlast that, and then the switch changes nothing. A later release will switch Codex at once without waiting.
- A switch that still restarts the gateway (Claude provider older than 0.3.1) refuses while anything runs, as before.

**After installing:** restart the gateway once, then fully close Hermes Desktop and open it again so it loads the new switch window.

The archive, its SHA-256 and the release gates are attached. Technical details are in `docs/release-notes.md`.
